items.title: Data Centers Must Disclose Erratic Power Use, Regulators Say
items.summary: As the data centers powering the AI boom grow larger and more numerous, they pose increasing challenges to the grid. Single facilities can draw as much power as a large city and their demand can lurch by hundreds of megawatts in seconds, straining the power grid . To rein in these wild electricity swings, U.S. regulators are beginning to write new rules. Their first step: Requiring data centers to disclose how their facilities interact with the grid, and just how wild their power swings are. To that end, the North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC), an international regulatory authority, in October adopted its first reliability standards for computational loads. top.title: Automated Design and Evaluation Pipeline for Optimal Control Transcriptions in Model Predictive Control
top.summary: The computational burden of Model Predictive Control represents a bottleneck limiting its widespread deployment in real-time applications. The selection of the optimal control transcription strategy for a given MPC formulation is a key driver of computational efficiency. Identifying performant MPC transcriptions requires significant effort and domain knowledge. We propose an automated pipeline for the design and evaluation of performant optimal control transcriptions for a given MPC formulation. Custom multi-objective design metrics, such as computation time or closed-loop performance, can be specified and are minimized by the pipeline. As a transcription method, a pseudospectral Legendre-Gauss-Radau method is employed. We show that it incorporates forward Euler integration and implicit collocation methods of low and high order in one formulation, leveraging the pipeline to evaluate both numerical approaches. top.title: MRCT: An Object-Centric Two-Layer Control Architecture for Heavy-Payload Multi-Robot Transportation
top.summary: Cooperative transportation of heavy payloads by heterogeneous mobile manipulators requires coordinated payload motion, force distribution, and compliant physical interaction. This paper presents MRCT, an object-centric two-layer control architecture for multi-robot transportation. At the object level, a model predictive controller (MPC) generates a coordinated contact-force reference for the payload. At the robot level, whole- body impedance control (WBIC) modules on individual robots realise the reference through a confidence-based blending of velocity-tracking and impedance torques. The blending mechanism emphasises tracking when the joint-velocity error is small and increases compliance when tracking degrades because of abrupt reference changes or physical disturbances. Simulation and hardware experiments with a heterogeneous team comprising a single-arm and a dual-arm mobile manipulator transporting a near-rated table payload demonstrate accurate object tracking, regulated contact
